steps.title: Lunch Break Talk · 월요일 점심, 회사 탕비실에서

lines.en: Ooh, that looks good! Hey, Jiwoo. {{What do you do in your free time}}?
lines.ko: 오, 맛있겠다! 참, 지우 씨. 시간 날 때 뭐 해요?

lines.en: I do yoga. {{I’m really into}} it these days.
lines.ko: 요가 해요. 요즘 요가에 푹 빠졌어요.

lines.en: “I’m really into it.” That sounded so natural! {{How often do you}} go?
lines.ko: “I’m really into it.” 정말 자연스러웠어요! 얼마나 자주 가요?

lines.en: Once a week. It helps me relax. What about you?
lines.ko: 일주일에 한 번요. 마음이 편해져요. 클로이는요?

lines.en: I love drawing. I draw almost every day. And I’ve just started climbing!
lines.ko: 저는 그림 그리기를 좋아해요. 거의 매일 그려요. 그리고 얼마 전에 암벽 등반을 시작했어요!

lines.en: Climbing? Wow! How did you get into it?
lines.ko: 등반이요? 와! 어떻게 시작하게 됐어요?

lines.en: A friend got me into it. Now I’m a member of an indoor climbing club.
lines.ko: 친구 덕분에 빠졌어요. 이제 실내 암벽 등반 동호회 회원이에요.

lines.en: Is it hard?
lines.ko: 어려워요?

lines.en: Yes! I’m not very good at it. I usually come down after a few meters.
lines.ko: 네! 아직 잘 못해요. 보통 몇 미터 올라가다 내려와요.

lines.en: Ha! {{How often do you}} go?
lines.ko: 하하! 얼마나 자주 가요?

lines.en: Not very often. Just on Thursdays. You should come with me sometime. Come on!
lines.ko: 자주는 아니에요. 목요일에만요. 언제 저랑 같이 가요. 자, 어서요!

lines.en: Hmm… okay! I’ll come to the club this Thursday.
lines.ko: 음… 좋아요! 이번 목요일에 동호회에 가 볼게요.

steps.title: Chloe’s Climbing Club
steps.text: Chloe joined an indoor climbing club last month. The membership is fairly cheap, and the club has many activities, like a craft night. Climbing fascinates her. She generally goes on Thursdays, *as soon as* she finishes work. The members are interesting. One is a musician and plays three instruments. Another is a singer. One member even has a collection of poems about climbing! For Chloe, every climb is a small victory. On weekends, some members go hiking on mountain trails. Jiwoo is curious now. She wants to *come to* the club this Thursday.
steps.gloss: membership 회원 자격 · fairly 꽤 · fascinate 마음을 사로잡다 · generally 대개 · as soon as ~하자마자 · victory 승리 · trail 산길 · curious 궁금한 · come to ~에 오다

steps.title: Home or Office? · 점심, 회사 근처 식당에서

lines.en: Jiwoo, my company is trying something new. We can work from home two days a week.
lines.ko: 지우, 우리 회사가 새로운 걸 시험해 보고 있어요. 일주일에 이틀은 집에서 일할 수 있어요.

lines.en: Oh, really? {{What do you think about}} it?
lines.ko: 오, 정말요? 마야는 그거 어떻게 생각해요?

lines.en: {{I think}} it’s a great idea. No crowded subway in the morning!
lines.ko: 좋은 생각 같아요. 아침에 붐비는 지하철을 안 타도 돼요!

lines.en: {{I think so, too}}. But is it good for the team? Hmm…
lines.ko: 저도 그렇게 생각해요. 그런데 팀한테도 좋을까요? 음…

lines.en: You’ve got this! Tell me your opinion.
lines.ko: 할 수 있어요! 지우 의견을 말해 봐요.

lines.en: Well, I think a team needs time together.
lines.ko: 음, 팀은 같이 있는 시간이 필요한 것 같아요.

lines.en: Why do you think so?
lines.ko: 왜 그렇게 생각해요?

lines.en: Good ideas often come at lunch or by the coffee machine.
lines.ko: 좋은 아이디어는 점심 때나 커피 머신 옆에서 자주 나오잖아요.

lines.en: Good point. But my boss is worried. He thinks people just relax at home.
lines.ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 그런데 우리 상사는 걱정해요. 사람들이 집에서 그냥 쉰다고 생각해요.

lines.en: {{I don’t think so}}. Many people work hard at home.
lines.ko: 저는 그렇게 생각 안 해요. 많은 사람이 집에서도 열심히 일해요.

lines.en: You’re right. Oh, and my heating bill may well go up this winter!
lines.ko: 맞아요. 아, 그리고 이번 겨울엔 난방비가 오를 것 같아요!

lines.en: That’s true! Make sure you wear a warm sweater.
lines.ko: 그렇겠네요! 따뜻한 스웨터 꼭 입어요.

steps.title: Maya’s Team Discussion
steps.text: Every Friday, Maya’s team has a short discussion. This week, the topic is working from home. Maya asks everybody to express an opinion. One member agrees with the plan. steps.title: Sam’s Visit
steps.text: Ben’s brother Sam came from Boston for a week. Jiwoo met him at a café. She didn’t know what he looked like, but Ben described his *appearance* — tall, glasses, a beard, *and so on*. So it was easy to identify him. Sam is nearly two meters tall, so he *looks down* at most people! He has a little gray in his beard. He is a nurse, and he *looks after* sick children. *In the long term*, he wants to work in Seoul. Before he left, he took a photo of himself with Ben and Jiwoo. “I’ll *look back* on this day and smile,” he said.

steps.title: Three Days in Busan
steps.text: Last week, Jiwoo went to Busan for three days. She *carried out* a big design project with a team there. She took a lot of documents in a big file. Grace, *on the other hand*, stayed in Seoul. She watered Jiwoo’s plants and took in her package. Then she sent a photo: “Your plants look happy. *Carry on* with your work!” On Friday, snow *held up* Jiwoo’s train. *At the time*, she was very tired, but she smiled. At home, she opened the box. In it, there was a small object: a new desk lamp. Then she knocked on Grace’s door with some snacks from Busan. “I owe you one!”

steps.title: Grace’s Bookshelf
steps.text: On Saturday, Grace’s new bookshelf came in a big, heavy box. Jiwoo helped her *take off* the plastic. Grace *takes on* a lot of work every week, so she was tired. After an hour, Jiwoo said, “Let me *take over*.” Grace directed, and Jiwoo did the hard parts. By evening, the bookshelf was complete. It *takes up* a whole wall, plus it has room for two hundred books! Grace also volunteers at a small library on Sundays. Next week, Jiwoo is going to go with her.

steps.title: Jiwoo’s Busy Week
steps.text: This week, Jiwoo has a big deadline. She has to finish a new web page by Friday at six. The project *takes up* all her time. At the Monday meeting, her team leader *brings up* the deadline again. *So far*, everything is going well. Jiwoo just has to *focus on* her work and organize her time. steps.title: Sunday at the Rink
steps.text: Every winter, the town *puts up* an outdoor skating rink near the park. It is open every day except Monday. Jiwoo and Ben wanted to go on Saturday morning, but Jiwoo suddenly had to work. It had *to do with* a client’s website. Changes like this occur all the time, and Ben didn’t mind. On Sunday, they met at two. They skated for an hour *or so*. Then Ben *pulled out* his phone and took a picture of Jiwoo with her hot chocolate. Next time, she is going to tell Ben about changes in advance.

lines.en: Thanks for the tip, Daniel!
lines.ko: 알려 줘서 고마워요, 대니얼!

steps.title: Jiwoo’s Reading Plan
steps.text: After coffee, Jiwoo visits a local bookstore and finds “Max and the Moon Café.” The author is not very famous, but the series is popular, and the reviews are great. The new edition is cheap because the price *went down* last month. Daniel’s tip was helpful because the book is easy and fun. Jiwoo wasn’t aware of the word list at the back, but now she can refer to it for new words. She reads ten pages *on her own* every day.

lines.en: Daniel, I need a new laptop for work. {{Which is better,}} this one {{or}} that one?
lines.ko: 대니얼, 일할 때 쓸 노트북이 필요해요. 이거랑 저거 중에 뭐가 더 나아요?

lines.en: Hmm. Compare these two. This model has a 13-inch screen. That one has a 16-inch screen.
lines.ko: 음. 이 둘을 비교해 봐요. 이 모델은 13인치 화면이고, 저건 16인치예요.

lines.en: Right. The big one has a wider screen, but the small one is much cheaper.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 큰 건 화면이 더 넓은데, 작은 게 훨씬 싸요.

lines.en: What about the other features?
lines.ko: 다른 기능은요?

lines.en: They’re about the same. Both are good.
lines.ko: 거의 같아요. 둘 다 좋아요.

lines.en: Then it depends. Do you carry it a lot?
lines.ko: 그럼 경우에 따라 달라요. 많이 들고 다녀요?

lines.en: Yes. To the office, to cafés, everywhere!
lines.ko: 네. 사무실에도, 카페에도, 어디든요!

lines.en: Then {{I think}} the small one {{is better}}. {{It’s}} light{{er than}} the big one.
lines.ko: 그럼 작은 게 더 나은 것 같아요. 큰 것보다 가벼워요.

lines.en: But I’m a designer. A big screen is easier for my work.
lines.ko: 하지만 전 디자이너예요. 큰 화면이 일하기 더 편해요.

lines.en: True. Neither is perfect. Is there a big monitor at your office?
lines.ko: 맞아요. 둘 다 완벽하진 않네요. 사무실에 큰 모니터 있어요?

lines.en: Yes, there is! Okay, I prefer the small one.
lines.ko: 네, 있어요! 좋아요, 작은 게 더 좋겠어요.

steps.teach: Sentence patterns: Which is better, ___ or ___? / I think ___ is better. It’s ___er than ___.. Using the table on screen, give the learner 2-3 situations from it and have them say the matching sentence. Then call next_step.

items:
짧은 말 + *-er*: light → lighter · fast → faster
-y로 끝나면: easy → easier
긴 말은 앞에 *more*: more comfortable · more convenient
따로 외워요: good → *better* · bad → *worse*

비교하는 대상 앞에 *than*: It’s lighter *than* the big one.
‘훨씬’은 *much*: It’s *much* cheaper.
‘~만큼 좋진 않아요’: It’s not as good as the big one.
errors: It’s lighter then the big one.
It’s lighter than the big one.
steps.teach: Explain the grammar points on screen very briefly (one or two sentences each, a short Korean explanation is OK), then quickly show the common mistakes: read the wrong sentence, ask the learner to fix it, then confirm. Then call next_step.
points: 비교급 만들기: 짧은 말 + -er: light → lighter · fast → faster-y로 끝나면: easy → easier긴 말은 앞에 more: more comfortable · more convenient따로 외워요: good → better · bad → worse
than · much: 비교하는 대상 앞에 than: It’s lighter than the big one.‘훨씬’은 much: It’s much cheaper.‘~만큼 좋진 않아요’: It’s not as good as the big one.
mistakes: It’s more cheaper. → It’s cheaper.
It’s lighter then the big one. → It’s lighter than the big one.
This one is gooder. → This one is better.

steps.title: Jiwoo’s New Laptop
steps.text: On Saturday, Jiwoo buys the small model. Despite its smaller screen, she loves it. It’s much lighter, so she can take it *all over* the city. steps.text: On Sunday, Jiwoo *wakes up* at six thirty. The bakery is *on the way* to the station, and Ben was right: you can’t miss it. There is a giant bread sign over the door. steps.title: Plan B
steps.text: On Saturday morning, the forecast indicated heavy rain. Daniel sent a text: “It’s raining. Plan B!” The rain determined their plan for the day. They met at the city museum. A small café *opened up* there last month, so they had lunch there. Later, the rain stopped, and they *got out* for a short walk. Then Jiwoo told Daniel her big news: she bought her plane ticket to Toronto! “Is it cold there in April?” “Sometimes it’s below zero,” said Daniel. “If that’s *the case*, I’ll bring a warm jacket.” “Good idea. And *bring back* some maple candy for me!”

steps.title: Our Building in the Dark
steps.text: Last night at nine, the lights went out in the whole neighborhood. During the blackout, the elevator stopped, so people used the stairs. Ben was walking home when it happened. steps.text: Maya plays in a soccer *league* for office workers. steps.title: Grace’s Checklist
steps.text: Jiwoo has been busy *recently*, so Grace made her a checklist. “Treat it *as though* it’s a game,” said Grace. “Finish one thing, then *move on* to the next.” Jiwoo has already done three things. She has booked a hotel, *signed up* for travel insurance, and *topped up* her travel card. But she hasn’t packed yet. Her room isn’t very *tidy*, so she *searched* the floor for her suitcase. At last, she *stood up*. There it was, on top of the closet! The last line says, “After the trip, *unpack* and rest.” Grace says, “Take small steps. You’ll feel calmer and be ready on time.”

steps.title: Time Travel
steps.text: After check-in at the airline counter, Jiwoo and Chloe go through security. A guard scans their bags. Oops! Jiwoo has a big bottle of water in her carry-on bag. Carry-on liquids must be in containers of 100 ml or less! At the gate, there’s an announcement, “Passengers for Toronto, please board now.” On the plane, the pilot says hello, and Jiwoo *finds herself* smiling. Her first international flight! Chloe watches Korean dramas throughout the flight. At the border, an officer asks, “Anything to declare?” “No, nothing.” They left Seoul in the morning, and it’s still morning in Toronto! “Don’t sleep now,” says Chloe. “*As long as* you stay awake till tonight, you’ll be fine.”
steps.gloss: airline 항공사 · guard 요원, 경비원 · scan (기계로) 검사하다 · liquid 액체 · announcement 안내 방송 · find oneself 어느새 ~하고 있다 · throughout ~ 내내 · declare (세관에) 신고하다 · as long as ~하기만 하면

steps.text: Chloe’s parents’ house is full this week. Some relations are visiting. So Jiwoo is staying at a small hotel near them. It has two wings, and her single room is in the new wing. steps.title: A Quiet Room
steps.text: After breakfast, Jiwoo moved to Room 508 *along with* her heavy suitcase. The new room was warm and quiet. The heater worked well, and there was plenty of hot water. Now let’s go see my city!”

steps.title: A Rainy Day Four
steps.text: It rained throughout the morning, so Chloe and Jiwoo went to a big museum. There was a room about old kings and queens. Jiwoo saw a royal crown and a small model of a castle. In the afternoon, the rain stopped *at last*. They *set out* for a beach by the lake. The sand was cold, but Jiwoo found a pretty shell. “My favorite souvenir!” she said. Then a wild animal ran across the path. It was a raccoon! Soon the wind got strong, so they *turned around* and went back to town. That night, Daniel sent a message: “I’m home in Chicago next week. Come and visit!” Maybe Jiwoo will.
